title: A transformation in Virgo
caption: The galaxy NGC 4388 in the Virgo Cluster, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4388 · constellation Virgo · about 60 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The outer parts of NGC 4388 look smooth and featureless, like an elliptical galaxy. Its center tells a different story. Dust lanes are held within two symmetric spiral arms that curl out from a glowing core, a clear mark of a spiral galaxy. Bright blue speckles in the arms show where young stars sit.

NGC 4388 is changing, and its mixed appearance reflects that. It lies some 60 million light-years away and belongs to the Virgo Cluster, a massive collection of over 1300 galaxies bound together by gravity. Life in such a crowded, massive cluster has some unwelcome effects on its members, and NGC 4388 is feeling them.
The young blue stars in its arms show that the galaxy has had recent bursts of star formation. The cluster is one reason the constellation Virgo (The Virgin) is so rich in galaxies.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.51 x 1.77 arcminutes) and distance (60 million light years), the frame spans roughly 44,000 × 31,000 light-years. Its light set out about 60 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed NGC 4388 in ultraviolet, blue and near-infrared light. Young stars appear blue, but the full color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of this light is ultraviolet or near-infrared, which the eye cannot see, and the galaxy is far too faint for unaided eyes.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 recorded NGC 4388 through ultraviolet, blue and near-infrared filters. The picture was released as an ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week. Its blend of elliptical and spiral features gives the galaxy a somewhat confused identity.
alt: A galaxy with a smooth, featureless outer glow and a center where dusty spiral arms dotted with blue young stars curl out from a bright core.
